```tsx
// app/api/chat/route.ts
import { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
})

export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  try {
    const { messages } = await req.json()

    if (!messages || !Array.isArray(messages)) {
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Invalid messages format' }), {
        status: 400,
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      })
    }

    if (!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY) {
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'OPENAI_API_KEY not configured' }), {
        status: 500,
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      })
    }

    // Create streaming response
    const stream = await openai.chat.completions.create({
      model: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4',
      messages,
      stream: true, // Enable streaming
    })

    // Return as Server-Sent Events (SSE)
    return new Response(
      new ReadableStream({
        async start(controller) {
          const encoder = new TextEncoder()
          for await (const chunk of stream) {
            const content = chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content
            if (content) {
              // Send as SSE format
              controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(`data: ${content}\
\
`))
            }
          }
          controller.close()
        },
      }),
      {
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
          'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
          'Connection': 'keep-alive',
        },
      }
    )
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Chat API error:', error)
    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Internal server error' }), {
      status: 500,
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    })
  }
}
```

```tsx
// pages/api/chat.ts
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
})

export default async function handler(
  req: NextApiRequest,
  res: NextApiResponse
) {
  if (req.method !== 'POST') {
    return res.status(405).json({ error: 'Method not allowed' })
  }

  try {
    const { messages } = req.body

    if (!messages || !Array.isArray(messages)) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Invalid messages format' })
    }

    if (!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY) {
      return res.status(500).json({ error: 'OPENAI_API_KEY not configured' })
    }

    // Set up SSE headers
    res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')
    res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-cache')
    res.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive')

    // Create streaming response
    const stream = await openai.chat.completions.create({
      model: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4',
      messages,
      stream: true,
    })

    // Stream chunks to client
    for await (const chunk of stream) {
      const content = chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content
      if (content) {
        res.write(`data: ${content}\
\
`)
      }
    }

    res.end()
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Chat API error:', error)
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' })
  }
}
```

```tsx
// server.ts
import express from 'express'
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const app = express()
app.use(express.json())

const openai = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
})

app.post('/api/chat', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const { messages } = req.body

    if (!messages || !Array.isArray(messages)) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Invalid messages format' })
    }

    if (!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY) {
      return res.status(500).json({ error: 'OPENAI_API_KEY not configured' })
    }

    // Set up SSE headers
    res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')
    res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-cache')
    res.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive')

    // Create streaming response
    const stream = await openai.chat.completions.create({
      model: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4',
      messages,
      stream: true,
    })

    // Stream chunks to client
    for await (const chunk of stream) {
      const content = chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content
      if (content) {
        res.write(`data: ${content}\
\
`)
      }
    }

    res.end()
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Chat API error:', error)
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' })
  }
})

app.listen(3000, () => {
  console.log('Server running on http://localhost:3000')
})

```tsx
import { useClarityChat, ChatWindow } from '@clarity-chat/react'

function Chat() {
  const { messages, append, isLoading } = useClarityChat({
    api: '/api/chat',
    // Streaming is enabled by default
  })

  return (
    <ChatWindow
      messages={messages}
      isLoading={isLoading}
      onSendMessage={async (content) => {
        await append({ role: 'user', content })
        // Response will stream automatically
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { StreamingMessage } from '@clarity-chat/react'

function Chat() {
  const [content, setContent] = useState('')
  const [isStreaming, setIsStreaming] = useState(false)

  // Handle streaming updates
  useEffect(() => {
    const eventSource = new EventSource('/api/chat')
    
    eventSource.onmessage = (event) => {
      setContent(prev => prev + event.data)
      setIsStreaming(true)
    }

    eventSource.onerror = () => {
      setIsStreaming(false)
      eventSource.close()
    }

    return () => eventSource.close()
  }, [])

  return (
    <StreamingMessage
      content={content}
      isStreaming={isStreaming}
      showThinking
      showCitations
    />
  )
}
```

# Vite Integration - Clarity Chat Components

### Mobile Guide

Add voice-to-text input to your chat application for hands-free interaction. Perfect for mobile apps, accessibility, and modern UX. Voice input uses the Web Speech API, which is supported in Chrome, Edge, and Safari. The component gracefully degrades on unsupported browsers. Quick Start Add voice input with just a few lines: } autoSubmit /> ) }`} /> With useClarityChat Integrate voice input with custom chat UI: ) } return ( ) }`} /> With AdvancedChatInput Combine voice input with text input: } autoSubmit size="lg" /> ) }`} /> Interim Results Show real-time transcription as the user speaks: } showInterim autoSubmit /> )} ) }`} /> Multi-Language Support Support multiple languages: setLanguage(e.target.value)} > ))} ) }`} /> Error Handling Handle errors gracefully: else if (error.includes('permission')) else if (error.includes('no-speech')) else }} autoSubmit /> ) }`} /> Browser Compatibility Check browser support before showing voice input: , []) if (!isSupported) return ( ) }`} /> Mobile Optimization Optimize for mobile devices: ) }`} /> Best Practices **Request permission early** - Ask for microphone permission on first use **Show visual feedback** - Use animations to indicate listening state **Handle errors gracefully** - Provide clear error messages **Support multiple languages** - Allow users to select their language **Show interim results** - Display real-time transcription **Auto-submit on speech end** - Improve UX by automatically sending **Check browser support** - Hide voice input on unsupported browsers Related VoiceInput Component Voice input component reference useVoiceInput Hook Voice input hook (lower level) Multi-Modal Chat Recipe Combine voice with other media Mobile Guide Mobile optimization guide
- **Request permission early** - Ask for microphone permission on first use **Show visual feedback** - Use animations to indicate listening state **Handle errors gracefully** - Provide clear error messages **Support multiple languages** - Allow users to select their language **Show interim results** - Display real-time transcription **Auto-submit on speech end** - Improve UX by automatically sending **Check browser support** - Hide voice input on unsupported browsers

> **Info**: Voice input uses the Web Speech API, which is supported in Chrome, Edge, and Safari. The component gracefully degrades on unsupported browsers.

```tsx
import { VoiceInput, ClarityChat } from '@clarity-chat/react'
import '@clarity-chat/react/styles.css'

function Chat() {
  return (
    <div>
      <ClarityChat api="/api/chat" />
      <VoiceInput
        onTranscript={(text) => {
          // Text is automatically sent to chat
          sendMessage(text)
        }}
        autoSubmit
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { useClarityChat, ChatWindow, VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'

function VoiceChat() {
  const { messages, append } = useClarityChat({
    api: '/api/chat',
  })

  const handleVoiceTranscript = async (text: string) => {
    await append({ role: 'user', content: text })
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <ChatWindow
        messages={messages}
        onSendMessage={handleVoiceTranscript}
      />
      <VoiceInput
        onTranscript={handleVoiceTranscript}
        autoSubmit
        showInterim
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { AdvancedChatInput, VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'

function ChatInput() {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <AdvancedChatInput
        value={message}
        onChange={setMessage}
        onSubmit={handleSend}
      />
      <VoiceInput
        onTranscript={(text) => {
          setMessage(text)
          handleSend(text)
        }}
        autoSubmit
        size="lg"
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'
import { useState } from 'react'

function VoiceChat() {
  const [interimText, setInterimText] = useState('')

  return (
    <div>
      <VoiceInput
        onTranscript={(text) => {
          setInterimText(text)
          // Final transcript will be sent when speech ends
        }}
        showInterim
        autoSubmit
      />
      {interimText && (
        <div className="interim-text italic text-gray-500">
          {interimText}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'
import { useState } from 'react'

function MultiLanguageChat() {
  const [language, setLanguage] = useState('en-US')

  const languages = [
    { code: 'en-US', name: 'English (US)' },
    { code: 'es-ES', name: 'Spanish' },
    { code: 'fr-FR', name: 'French' },
    { code: 'de-DE', name: 'German' },
    { code: 'ja-JP', name: 'Japanese' },
  ]

  return (
    <div>
      <select
        value={language}
        onChange={(e) => setLanguage(e.target.value)}
      >
        {languages.map(lang => (
          <option key={lang.code} value={lang.code}>
            {lang.name}
          </option>
        ))}
      </select>
      <VoiceInput
        onTranscript={handleTranscript}
        lang={language}
        autoSubmit
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'

function VoiceChat() {
  return (
    <VoiceInput
      onTranscript={handleTranscript}
      onError={(error) => {
        if (error.includes('not supported')) {
          toast.error('Voice input is not supported in this browser')
        } else if (error.includes('permission')) {
          toast.error('Microphone permission denied. Please enable it in your browser settings.')
        } else if (error.includes('no-speech')) {
          toast.error('No speech detected. Please try again.')
        } else {
          toast.error('Voice input error: ' + error)
        }
      }}
      autoSubmit
    />
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'

function VoiceChat() {
  const [isSupported, setIsSupported] = useState(false)

  useEffect(() => {
    // Check if Web Speech API is supported
    setIsSupported(
      'webkitSpeechRecognition' in window ||
      'SpeechRecognition' in window
    )
  }, [])

  if (!isSupported) {
    return (
      <div className="text-gray-500">
        Voice input is not supported in this browser.
        Please use Chrome, Edge, or Safari.
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <VoiceInput
      onTranscript={handleTranscript}
      autoSubmit
    />
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { VoiceInput } from '@clarity-chat/react'

function MobileVoiceChat() {
  return (
    <VoiceInput
      onTranscript={handleTranscript}
      autoSubmit
      size="lg" // Larger button for mobile
      showTooltip
      tooltipText="Tap to speak"
      className="fixed bottom-4 right-4 rounded-full shadow-lg"
    />
  )
}
```

# Conversation Branching Example - Clarity Chat Components

# Conversation Branching

## Overview

## Live Demo

## Tips

Give reviewers and power users the ability to explore alternative responses, compare iterations, and merge winning paths back into the main conversation. Overview This example pairs `ConversationBranchVisualizer` with `useBranchManagement` and the standard `ChatWindow`. Users can fork from any message, rename branches, and jump between paths without losing context. Create, rename, and delete branches inline. Highlight the active branch path so users never lose track. Persist branch metadata for analytics (message counts, last message preview, token usage). Live Demo \`, role: 'assistant', content }, ]) } return ( ) } render()`} /> Tips Store branches in your database (e.g., Postgres, Supabase, Firestore) and hydrate `useBranchManagement` on mount. Branch metadata can power reports for red teaming and QA.
- Create, rename, and delete branches inline. Highlight the active branch path so users never lose track. Persist branch metadata for analytics (message counts, last message preview, token usage).

> **Info**: Store branches in your database (e.g., Postgres, Supabase, Firestore) and hydrate `useBranchManagement` on mount. Branch metadata can power reports for red teaming and QA.

The AI isn't just chatting — it's orchestrating. Watch it call tools, render interactive UI, and ask for your approval on critical actions. Generative UI Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Step Chains Glass Box Debugging Tool Chains AI calls Tool A, analyzes result, then decides to call Tool B Generative UI Tool calls render live React components, not just JSON Human-in-the-Loop Critical actions require your explicit approval Glass Box Debug See the AI's thought process in real-time Live Demo How It Works 1. Multi-Step Tool Chains When you ask "Analyze Apple stock", the AI doesn't just call one tool. It orchestrates a chain: **search_ticker** → Finds the correct symbol (AAPL) **get_financials** → Fetches price, P/E ratio, market cap **render_chart** → Generates an interactive price chart Each step builds on the previous one. The AI analyzes results and decides what to do next. 2. Generative UI Instead of returning raw JSON, each tool renders a custom React component. This is the heart of "Generative UI": `)`}` 3. # Bundle & Performance Analysis - Developer Tools

Use the built-in analysis and benchmarking scripts to monitor bundle size, performance, and regression drift.

# Bundle & Performance Analysis

## Commands

## Outputs

## Bundle Analysis Script

## Benchmark Script

## Integrating with CI

Keep bundle size and runtime performance under control with repeatable scripts that generate HTML dashboards and regression reports. Commands Outputs `bundle-reports/bundle-report.html` — per-package size breakdown with history comparisons `benchmark-results/benchmark-report.html` — latency statistics (mean, p95, p99) for key operations JSON counterparts for both reports (use in CI dashboards or Grafana) Bundle Analysis Script The analyze script traverses every workspace package, measures ESM/CJS/UMD bundles, and compares them with the previous report. Commit the latest `bundle-report.json` to your telemetry pipeline to graph bundle size over time. Benchmark Script Benchmarks simulate heavy operations (JSON parsing, array filtering, deep cloning) with warmup runs and 100 iterations.
- `bundle-reports/bundle-report.html` — per-package size breakdown with history comparisons `benchmark-results/benchmark-report.html` — latency statistics (mean, p95, p99) for key operations JSON counterparts for both reports (use in CI dashboards or Grafana) Bundle Analysis Script The analyze script traverses every workspace package, measures ESM/CJS/UMD bundles, and compares them with the previous report. Commit the latest `bundle-report.json` to your telemetry pipeline to graph bundle size over time. Benchmark Script Benchmarks simulate heavy operations (JSON parsing, array filtering, deep cloning) with warmup runs and 100 iterations. Extend the script with your own benchmarks (e.g. streaming throughput, serialization) to track domain-specific performance budgets. Integrating with CI Run `npm run analyze` + `npm run benchmark` in every PR Upload HTML/JSON reports as artifacts (see the CI/CD guide) Alert when bundle growth exceeds thresholds (size-limit fails the build) Feed JSON output into Grafana/Datadog for trends

> **Tip**: Commit the latest `bundle-report.json` to your telemetry pipeline to graph bundle size over time. Extend the script with your own benchmarks (e.g. streaming throughput, serialization) to track domain-specific performance budgets.

# CI/CD Reference Pipeline

## Workflow Overview

## GitHub Actions Workflow

## Pre-Commit Hooks

The repository includes a production-ready CI/CD recipe tested during the “CI/CD Final Status” audit. Use it as-is or tailor it to your platform. Workflow Overview 🔁 Trigger on PRs to `main` and on every push 🏗️ Jobs: lint, unit tests, Playwright, typecheck, bundle analysis 📦 Caches: Turbo repo + npm for repeatable builds 📜 Artifacts: bundle-report, benchmark-report, Playwright traces 🚀 Deployment: Vercel preview builds + manual promotion to production Review the [ CI_CD_FINAL_STATUS.md ](https://github.com/christireid/Clarity-ai-chat-components/blob/main/CI_CD_FINAL_STATUS.md) on GitHub for the original audit notes, pass/fail logs, and recommendations. GitHub Actions Workflow Pre-Commit Hooks Husky + lint-staged ensure code quality before it hits CI. This keeps your pipeline fast and reduces noise. Deployment **Docs Site**: `npm run docs:build` > deploy via Vercel (`vercel deploy --prod apps/docs`) **Marketing Site**: same pipeline, different workspace **Packages**: use Changesets `npm run release` to version + publish Secrets & Config Store provider keys in platform secrets (Vercel, GitHub Actions, HashiCorp Vault). The `clarity-chat doctor` command validates required environment variables before deploy.
- 🔁 Trigger on PRs to `main` and on every push 🏗️ Jobs: lint, unit tests, Playwright, typecheck, bundle analysis 📦 Caches: Turbo repo + npm for repeatable builds 📜 Artifacts: bundle-report, benchmark-report, Playwright traces 🚀 Deployment: Vercel preview builds + manual promotion to production Review the [ CI_CD_FINAL_STATUS.md ](https://github.com/christireid/Clarity-ai-chat-components/blob/main/CI_CD_FINAL_STATUS.md) on GitHub for the original audit notes, pass/fail logs, and recommendations. # @clarity-chat/codemods - Developer Tools

Automated jscodeshift transforms for upgrading Clarity Chat projects safely.

# @clarity-chat/codemods

## Installation

## Common Commands

## Transforms Included

## Before & After Preview

## Tips

## Extending

Upgrade across major versions without manually touching hundreds of files. These codemods are the same ones we run internally during releases. Installation Common Commands v2 migration (no changes written) clarity-codemod run v1-to-v2 ./src --dry --print # Apply migration clarity-codemod run v1-to-v2 ./src # Chain multiple migrations (v1 -> v3) clarity-codemod migrate 1 3 ./src --dry clarity-codemod migrate 1 3 ./src`} /> Always commit before running codemods and start with `--dry` +`--print`. The tool preserves formatting/comments, but version control is your safety net. Transforms Included **v1-to-v2** — renames props, updates component names, adjusts config schema **v2-to-v3** — (example) reorganises streaming APIs, updates token helpers **Custom** — add your own by registering transforms in `src/transforms` Before & After Preview console.log(msg)} config=} /> // After (v2) import from '@clarity-chat/react' console.log(msg)} config= }} /> `} /> Tips Run lint and tests after applying transforms Use `--parser` to switch between `babel`, `ts`, and `tsx` as needed Add `--verbose` for detailed logs when debugging Extending Codemods are powered by jscodeshift. Create a new transform file, export a`Transform`, and register it in `src/transforms/index.ts`. Use the provided tests as a template for coverage.
- **v1-to-v2** — renames props, updates component names, adjusts config schema **v2-to-v3** — (example) reorganises streaming APIs, updates token helpers **Custom** — add your own by registering transforms in `src/transforms` Before & After Preview console.log(msg)} config=} /> // After (v2) import from '@clarity-chat/react' console.log(msg)} config= }} /> `} /> Tips Run lint and tests after applying transforms Use `--parser` to switch between `babel`, `ts`, and `tsx` as needed Add `--verbose` for detailed logs when debugging

```tsx
import {
  ClarityChat,
  autoOptimize,
  PromptCacheManager,
  useTokenOptimization
} from '@clarity-chat/react'

// 1. Set up prompt caching
const cacheManager = new PromptCacheManager({
  provider: 'anthropic',
  strategy: 'aggressive'
})

// 2. Optimize structured data with TOON
function prepareContext(data) {
  const { formatted, metadata } = autoOptimize(data)
  console.log(`Saved ${metadata.tokensSaved} tokens`)
  return formatted
}

// 3. Use token optimization hook
function ChatWithOptimization() {
  const { optimizedMessages, stats } = useTokenOptimization({
    maxTokens: 8000,
    strategy: 'smart-truncation'
  })

  return (
    <ClarityChat
      messages={optimizedMessages}
      cacheManager={cacheManager}
      onTokenUsage={(usage) => console.log(usage)}
    />
  )
}
```

# About Clarity Chat

) } export const metadata: Metadata = export default function AboutPage() Our Mission We believe that building AI chat interfaces should be a joy, not a chore. Too many developers waste weeks rebuilding the same chat components from scratch, fighting with accessibility, wrestling with state management, and battling performance issues. Clarity Chat was born from this frustration. We set out to create the most complete, production-ready chat component library that handles all the hard parts—so you can focus on building unique AI experiences for your users. Our Values Developer Experience First Every decision we make prioritizes your experience. From comprehensive TypeScript support to clear documentation, we want you to ship faster and with confidence. Accessibility for All WCAG AAA compliance isn't optional—it's built into every component. Everyone deserves access to great AI chat experiences, regardless of ability. Open Source MIT licensed and community-driven. We believe great tools should be accessible to everyone, and better together through open collaboration. Performance Matters Virtual scrolling, tree-shaking, React.memo optimization—we obsess over performance so your users enjoy fast, responsive chat experiences. 200+ Components 140+ Hooks 249K+ Lines of Code 100% TypeScript Open Source Clarity Chat is built and maintained by a passionate community of developers who believe in creating better tools for everyone. We welcome contributions from developers of all skill levels. View on GitHub Contributing Guide Join Us Whether you're building your first chat interface or scaling to millions of users, we're here to help you succeed.
